kids: Watch lit boats glide along the Intracoastal
Spot decorated docks along the shore
Wave to the crews from the bridge viewing area
site: Parade runs from one mile south of the bridge toward Marsh Landing
about: The parade began in 1993 with a handful of spirited boats and cheering neighbors, and the committee says it has grown into one of Palm Valley's most loved holiday traditions.
Power boats over 30 feet, power boats under 30 feet and sailboats can register, and a separate dock decorating competition is open to waterfront homes.
The event is fully volunteer powered, and the organizers accept donations through an official PayPal page and invite sponsors.
St. Johns County Parks and Recreation and the Palm Valley Community Association are the presenting partners.
Boat and dock rules cover the gathering point, speed, spacing and VHF communications, and the committee takes questions through a contact page.
Some parking, shuttle and accessibility details on the viewing page were still being updated for 2026.
faq: When is the Palm Valley Boat Parade?
Saturday, December 5, 2026, with lights on at 6 PM.
Is it free to watch?
Yes, the organizers say everyone is invited to watch for free.
Where do we watch?
The Palm Valley Bridge viewing area is a favorite gathering place, so bring a chair and arrive early.
Which way does the parade travel?
It starts one mile south of the Palm Valley Bridge and heads north toward Marsh Landing.
Can our boat or dock join?
Yes, 2026 registration is open for power boats, sailboats and docks.
How long has this been going?
Since 1993.

kids: See the Holy Family journey re-enacted
Learn how Las Posadas began in 16th century Mexico
Spend an Advent evening at the historic mission
site: National Shrine of Our Lady of La Leche
Mission Nombre de Dios at 101 San Marco Avenue
about: The shrine's event page is titled Las Posadas: A Christmas Tradition, and the shrine's home page promotes it as Una Noche de Navidad, A Christmas Night.
The shrine describes itself as America's oldest Marian shrine, set on the grounds of Mission Nombre de Dios, where it says the Catholic faith took root in America in 1565.
Tickets are handled through an online ministry form linked on the event page, and a flyer can be downloaded from the same page.
The page offers add to calendar links for Google, iCal and Outlook.
Related events at the shrine on nearby dates include Meet Catholic Authors sessions on Saturdays from 1 to 3 PM.
faq: When is Las Posadas at the shrine?
Saturday, December 12, 2026, from 3 to 8 PM.
Where is it?
At the National Shrine of Our Lady of La Leche, 101 San Marco Avenue, St. Augustine.
What is Las Posadas?
A tradition from 16th century Mexico that re-enacts the Holy Family's journey from Nazareth to Bethlehem.
Do I need a ticket?
The event page links a ticket form, so register there.
How much does it cost?
The event page lists no price.
Is there a flyer?
Yes, a flyer titled Una Noche de Navidad is linked on the event page.

kids: Meet re-enactors in an 18th century encampment
See muskets fired in Colonial Quarter demonstrations
Follow the torches down St. George Street
site: Torchlight parade to the Governor's House
about: Public days are Friday, December 4 and Saturday, December 5, from 10 AM to 4 PM at the Oldest House Museum.
The encampment recreates 1739 through 1785, when Spanish forces and their allies and British forces and their allies were in St. Augustine.
Scheduled presentations run Saturday from 11 AM to 3 PM, and Colonial Quarter programs for the public run from 10 AM to 5 PM that day.
The torchlight parade starts at the Visitor Information Center at 7 PM, passes through the City Gates and ends at the Governor's House at King Street and St. George Street.
Visit St. Augustine explains that after the city gates were locked at night, people on the streets had to carry a light so the Night Watch could identify them.
A jollification party for participants follows at the Oldest House Museum after the parade.
The tourism board suggests earplugs for guests who are sensitive to the musket salute.
faq: When is the Colonial Night Watch?
Friday, December 4 and Saturday, December 5, 2026, with public days from 10 AM to 4 PM.
When is the torchlight parade?
Saturday, December 5, at 7 PM from the Visitor Information Center.
Where does the parade end?
At the Governor's House, 48 King Street.
Where is the encampment?
At the Oldest House Museum, 14 Francis Street.
Will there be musket fire?
Yes, and the tourism board suggests earplugs for sensitive ears.
How much is admission?
The organizer's page lists no price.
